findings.title: Login-cache invalidation on update uses the org-aware wrapped model, so changes to IDPs of disabled orgs are missed
findings.body:
In `update()`, `idpById` comes from `getById()`, which returns the model wrapped by `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel`. That wrapper's `isEnabled()` returns false whenever the linked organization is disabled. The cached login lists, however, are built from `idpDelegate.getForLogin`, which only checks the IDP's own `enabled` column. So IDPs of a disabled org are in the cached sets; this is why the bean now re-checks `isEnabled()`.

Scenario: org A is disabled and has a public, enabled IDP X that sits in the `ALL`/`ORG_ONLY` login cache. An admin sets X's `BROKER_PUBLIC` to false (or `hideOnLogin` / `linkOnly` to true). `getLoginPredicate().test(original)` is false because of the wrapper, and `test(updated)` is also false, so the early return at line 405 skips invalidation. When org A is re-enabled, which does not touch the login keys, the stale cached set still contains X. `getById` returns a fresh model whose `isEnabled()` is now true, and the bean only re-checks `isEnabled()`. A private, hidden or link-only broker is then shown on the login page until something else invalidates the cache.

Fix: evaluate the predicate against the raw stored model, e.g. `idpDelegate.getById(...)` or the unwrapped cached model, as `remove()` already does with `idpDelegate.getByAlias`.

findings.title: Merge path can re-cache stale per-org results after a concurrent invalidation
Single cache entry per FetchMode shared across all organizations causes churn and unbounded growth
findings.body: `cacheKeyForLogin` keys only on realm and mode, while `organizationId` is stored as a searchKey inside one `IdentityProviderListQuery`. Every first login lookup for a not-yet-seen organization invalidates and rebuilds the whole entry for that mode, merging in all previous orgs' sets. In realms with many organizations, this causes repeated invalidation of the shared entry. Concurrent lookups for different orgs race and drop each other's results. The entry also grows roughly as (#orgs × #realm-level login IDPs) for `ALL` mode. Including the organization id in the cache key would avoid both problems.

findings.title: Test cleanup removes literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDPs
findings.body: `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)` registers a cleanup for an IDP whose alias is literally "alias". It does not target the `idp-alias-N` providers created in the loop, and line 425 repeats the same mistake for `idp-alias-20`. None of the created IDPs are cleaned up by these registrations, and the cleanup targets a non-existent resource. The cleanup should use the actual alias, e.g. `get("idp-alias-" + i)`.
